ascon-cw-unprotected.notes: 100,000 software power traces collected from an unprotected Ascon implementation on a ChipWhisperer STM32F4 target. Two groups: random_keys (profiling) and fixed_keys (attack). NOTE: the file also ships a precomputed per-trace 'labels' (N,64) array; the benchmark ignores it and computes labels from the metadata (nonce+key). That shipped array could not be reproduced from the metadata under any standard Ascon convention - it uses an undocumented internal bit/word packing - so do not rely on it; it does not affect the traces or metadata, which are correct.

ascadf.notes: Fixed-key ASCAD package containing synchronized raw traces, processed ASCAD datasets, desynchronized variants, and trained reference models.

aes-hd-git.notes: GitHub CSV variant with 100,000 unprocessed traces split across five trace files plus labels, pinned to upstream commit 8baa486eeb38a043ed4dafadf55bcd03e8846def.

aes-hd-zaid.notes: Preprocessed AES HD NumPy archive used with the efficient-CNN methodology, pinned to the commit that introduced the current artifact.

eshard-aes-masked-non-shuffled.notes: Electromagnetic traces from a Boolean-masked software AES implementation on an STM32F4 Cortex-M4, acquired without SubBytes operation shuffling. The 135,112,903-byte ETS artifact is pinned to upstream commit f2c615e14c6f157d79a5f4b01fdf0537e910705d. No license is stated; the authors' README presents the data as a research resource and invites researchers to contact eShard with ideas and results.

eshard-aes-masked-shuffled.notes: Electromagnetic traces from a Boolean-masked software AES implementation on an STM32F4 Cortex-M4, with shuffled SubBytes operations. The 136,043,104-byte ETS artifact is pinned to upstream commit f2c615e14c6f157d79a5f4b01fdf0537e910705d. WARNING: this file is not consistent. Its 100,000 traces, keys, masks and ciphertexts are identical to those of eshard-aes-masked-non-shuffled; only the plaintexts (and an added permutation column) differ, and AES(plaintext, key) matches none of the ciphertexts (checked September 2026). The ciphertext problem is reported upstream as open issue #2 (https://gitlab.com/eshard/nucleo_sw_aes_masked_shuffled/-/issues/2, October 2023). Do not use it as a separate shuffled acquisition until the authors correct it. No license is stated; the authors' README presents the data as a research resource and invites researchers to contact eShard with ideas and results.

portability.notes: Power traces for the NDSS 2020 portability benchmark. AES-128 software implementation, 600 time samples per trace, multiple devices for realistic cross-device profiled side-channel analysis.

metadata.scope: device c1_k1; fixed key K1 in KEY LIST.txt (not in .mat)

galactics-attack-data.notes: GALACTICS side-channel benchmark archive containing the BLISS-A and BLISS-B profiling datasets together with the corresponding attack traces and metadata. The archive is distributed as a single 7z file.

metadata.security: PICKLE: unpickling executes arbitrary code; requires trust_pickle=True at load time
metadata.note: traces in pandas-pickled DataFrames; targets: Kx_const/z_cflip/sc_cflip/yu (per device_a/b attack folders). Set member to another *.pickle to pick a different target/device.

kyber-reference-ppm.notes: 100,000 fixed-key power traces, each with 50,000 samples, captured from unprotected pair-pointwise multiplication during CRYSTALS-Kyber decapsulation on a Cortex-M4 target. Confirmed on the real file: dataset.labels (MATLAB noncesA) is (n, 12) = two 6-value blocks [sk_lo, sk_hi, in_lo, in_hi, out_lo, out_hi]; sk is the fixed secret NTT coefficient (block 0 = 558, block 1 = 17), in the known ciphertext input (varies), and out = fqmul(sk, in) = montgomery_reduce(sk*in) (Q=3329, QINV=62209) verified bit-exact.

ge-wars.notes: GE Wars: The Deep Learning SCA Battle public dataset with 500,000 profiling and 100,000 attack electromagnetic traces in an ASCAD-like HDF5 layout. Measurements target the first byte after AddRoundKey in the first AES-128 round on an unprotected Raspberry Pi 4B with a Broadcom BCM2711 quad-core ARM Cortex-A72 processor.

ecc-dataset.notes: Electromagnetic side-channel dataset targeting the CSWAP-pointer implementation of Curve25519 on a 32-bit ARM Cortex-M4F. The dataset contains 300 traces (250 profiling and 50 attack), each with 1,000 samples. The implementation uses a constant-time Montgomery ladder with coordinate re-randomization and a fresh random scalar for every scalar multiplication.

aes-ptv2-pinata.notes: Power side-channel dataset collected on a Riscure Piñata STM32F4 Cortex-M4F. The Piñata subset contains 150,000 traces (100,000 profiling and 50,000 attack), each with 1,260 samples stored in HDF5 format. The repository also includes four identical devices (D1–D4), each with datasets acquired without countermeasures and with masking schemes MS1 and MS2, using both fixed and random keys.

ches-ctf-2018.notes: Power side-channel dataset from the CHES CTF 2018 challenge. Contains 50,000 HDF5 traces (45,000 profiling and 5,000 attack), each with 2,200 samples, acquired from a 32-bit STM microcontroller running a first-order XOR Boolean-masked AES-128 implementation with a fixed key.

metadata.note: labels are in each wave filename: k=key, m=plaintext, c=ciphertext (16 bytes each, verified AES(m,k)=c). The public base has 640,000 traces under 32 keys, 20,000 traces per key. Hardware AES leaks best under a last-round Hamming-distance model.

dpacontest-v4-1-rsm.notes: DPA Contest v4.1 AES-256 RSM benchmark. The dataset consists of the dpav4_rsm_index file and twenty ZIP archives containing the traces. dpacontest-v4-2.notes: DPA Contest v4.2 benchmark. Downloads the index file together with the 32 ZIP archives containing the traces: 80,000 traces under 16 keys, 5,000 traces per key (checked against the index and the official traces page). Known implementation issues, from the official documentation (https://dpacontest.telecom-paris.fr/v4/42_doc.php): the traces were updated in July 2015 and no longer contain the first bug found (October 2014), but they still contain the second one (August 2015): 'the permutation function Shuffle10 is used before the first round instead of Shuffle0'. The mask set used differs from the published description (page 4 of the SPACE 2014 paper): [0x03, 0x0c, 0x35, 0x3a, 0x50, 0x5f, 0x66, 0x69, 0x96, 0x99, 0xa0, 0xaf, 0xc5, 0xca, 0xf3, 0xfc]. Users of these traces are asked to cite 'RSM: A small and fast countermeasure for AES, secure against 1st and 2nd-order zero-offset SCAs' (DATE 2012). No license is stated; the DPA Contest site says its data and code "apply to the evaluation of academic, unprotected and whitebox cryptographic implementations" and are not meant to encourage piracy on commercial hardware.

ches-ctf-2018-challenge-2.notes: CHES CTF 2018 Challenge 2 dataset collected on a Riscure Pinata platform. The benchmark comprises four 10k-trace acquisition files together with two additional 1k no-key acquisition files, distributed as six TRS files. In the two no-key files (PinataAcqTask2.5_1k_NK and 2.6_1k_NK) the key field is all zeros: the key is not provided, so do not compute labels from it (checked on the files, September 2026). Files 2.1 to 2.3 use a new key per trace and 2.4 one fixed key.

aes-rd.notes: Power traces from an AES-128 implementation protected with random delay insertion on an Atmel ATmega16 microcontroller. The MATLAB file contains 50,000 traces of 3,500 samples each and is the dataset accompanying Kizhvatov's random-delay countermeasure studies.

wolfssl-ed25519.notes: Power side-channel dataset targeting the WolfSSL Ed25519 implementation (Curve25519) used in 'One Trace Is All It Takes: Machine Learning-Based Side-Channel Attack on EdDSA'. The repository distributes a single HDF5 file (databaseEdDSA.h5) containing the profiling dataset used in the paper.

reassure-c25519-arithm.notes: Electromagnetic side-channel traces of the μNaCl Curve25519 Montgomery ladder on a Riscure Piñata STM32F4 target. The implementation uses arithmetic-based conditional swap together with projective-coordinate re-randomization and scalar randomization. The collection contains an aligned 5,997-trace dataset, a 100-trace aligned subset, and the corresponding 100 full traces.

metadata.note: pattern-extracted aligned sub-traces (5500 samples); 1-byte label = Montgomery-ladder swap bit

re-encryption.notes: Re-encryption distinguishing dataset (Ueno et al., ePrint 2021/849). The default folder (aes_nonprotect_sw) holds power traces of an unprotected software AES-128 used as the PRF inside a Fujisaki-Okamoto re-encryption, on an STM32F415 (Cortex-M4). Other folders: SHAKE software, AES and masked AES hardware on a Kintex-7 FPGA (power), and masked AES software on an STM32F407 (EM). The task is fixed-vs-random plaintext distinguishing with a fixed key. The unprotected sets hold 50,000 traces with a predefined split and 1,000 features.

metadata.note: distinguishing attack: label 0=fixed, 1=random; base_dir selects one of aes_masked_hw/sw, aes_nonprotect_hw/sw, keccak_nonprotect_sw, ntru_nonprotect_sw; split=train|test

dfs-desynch.notes: Power side-channel dataset containing 256,000 highly desynchronized traces of an unprotected OpenSSL AES-128 software implementation running on a 32-bit RISC-V SoC implemented on an AMD Artix-7 FPGA. Dynamic Frequency Scaling randomly changes the operating frequency among 35, 40, 45, 50, 55 and 60 MHz. The dataset contains 128,000 profiling and 128,000 attack traces, each with 200,000 samples acquired at 125 MS/s with 12-bit resolution. Data are stored in HDF5 and partitioned into 32 chunks according to the first AES key byte: each chunk holds 8 keys (one per first-key-byte value), so 256 keys in total, in both splits. Each split also holds a 'labels' dataset that is not a class label but the clock-frequency schedule, records of (sample, frequency); it is not exposed as labels (checked on the file, October 2026). Compute labels from the keys and plaintexts.

dtds-dilithium2.notes: Dilithium2 subset of DTDS: Dilithium Dataset for Power Analysis. 12 chunks x 5000 = 60,000 signing traces; per chunk polyz_unpack_traces.npy is (5000, 20000) int16 and polyz_unpack_y.npy is (5000, 4, 256) int32 = the masking polynomial y (4 polys x 256 coeffs, values in [-(gamma1-1), gamma1], gamma1=2^17). Confirmed on the real file: each 20000-sample trace covers polyz_unpack of polynomial 0 only (its 256 coefficients, ~75 samples each; polys 1-3 do not leak in these traces). key/pk/msg live in mate.req, not exposed as a field.

metadata.note: key material (sk/pk/msg) is in mate.req, not exposed as a field

ascadv.notes: ASCAD variable-key (ATMega8515) synchronized extracted traces in the ASCAD HDF5 layout (Profiling_traces/Attack_traces + metadata plaintext/key/masks); the key varies per trace.

ascadv-desync50.notes: ASCAD variable-key extracted traces with a maximum desynchronization of 50 samples.

ascadv-desync100.notes: ASCAD variable-key extracted traces with a maximum desynchronization of 100 samples.

ascadv-raw.notes: ASCAD variable-key raw acquisition (~75 GB): root-level 'traces' plus a compound 'metadata' record (plaintext/key/masks). No pre-extracted window or profiling/attack split. The file holds 300,001 records of 250,000 samples; the last one (index 300000) is all zeros, trace and metadata (checked on the file, September 2026), so drop it before use, as for the ASCADv2 raw files.

ascadv2.notes: ASCADv2: affine-masked AES-128 on an STM32 (ARM Cortex-M4). Extracted ASCAD-style HDF5 (Profiling_traces/Attack_traces + metadata; richer mask fields). Auto-downloaded (7.7 GB), verified against the authoritative ANSSI sha1 published at object.files.data.gouv.fr/anssi/ascadv2/sha1.txt. WARNING: per the ANSSI notice, profiling traces 99999/199999/299999/399999/499999 are zeroed by an acquisition issue (the attack part is clean) - drop those before training to avoid bias. Eight raw acquisition files (ascadv2-stm32-conso-raw-traces1..8.h5) are the separate ascadv2r entry. Adapter mapping is ASCAD-format, checked on the real file (September 2026).

aes-ptv2-pinata-ms1.notes: AES-PTv2 Piñata, masking scheme MS1 (same .h5 as the unprotected Piñata set; loads the MS1 implementation groups).

aes-ptv2-pinata-ms2.notes: AES-PTv2 Piñata, masking scheme MS2 (same .h5 as the unprotected Piñata set; loads the MS2 implementation groups).

aes-ptv2-stm32f4-ms1.notes: AES-PTv2 STM32F4 (device D1), masking scheme MS1 (same device .h5 files as the unprotected set).

aes-ptv2-stm32f4-ms2.notes: AES-PTv2 STM32F4 (device D1), masking scheme MS2 (same device .h5 files as the unprotected set).

ecc-cswap-arith.notes: Curve25519 CSWAP-arithmetic variant; ships in the same ecc_datasets.zip as the registered CSWAP-pointer entry (loads cswap_arith.h5).

ascon-cw-protected.notes: First-order Domain-Oriented-Masking protected Ascon on a ChipWhisperer STM32F4 (same Zenodo record as the unprotected set).

ascon-cw-unprotected-raw.notes: Raw (Riscure .trs) unprotected Ascon acquisition (same Zenodo record). Loaded traces-only; the per-trace crypto-data byte layout is not yet mapped.

ascad-raw-fixed.notes: ASCAD fixed-key RAW acquisition: ATMega8515_raw_traces.h5 (5.6 GB, 60,000 traces x 100,000 samples), shipped inside the same ASCAD_data.zip as the extracted ascadf set. Root-level 'traces' + compound 'metadata' (plaintext/key/masks).

ascadv2r.notes: ASCADv2 RAW acquisition (STM32F303, shuffling + affine masking): eight ascadv2-stm32-conso-raw-traces{1..8}.h5 files, 100,000 encryptions each (~100 GB per file, ~800 GB total). Auto-downloaded and verified against the authoritative ANSSI sha1 (object.files.data.gouv.fr/anssi/ascadv2/sha1.txt); mind the size (~100 GB per file, ~800 GB total); download only some files with files=, e.g. files='*traces1.h5'. WARNING: per the ANSSI notice, the last trace of each raw file (and its metadata) is zeroed by an acquisition issue - drop it before use to avoid bias. Adapter config (root-level 'traces' + 'metadata' compound with plaintext/key/masks columns) verified against ANSSI's ASCAD_generate.py.
